title: Shared-facility hygiene and tenant notice
audience: Cleaners who clean shared facilities such as laundries, gyms, pools and bin rooms, and who give tenants notice.
learningOutcomes: Clean shared facilities with approved methods and dedicated tools.
Give tenants notice of work and closures in the agreed way.
Report damage, contamination and unsafe conditions in shared facilities.

instruction.heading: Shared facilities and why hygiene matters
instruction.body:
Shared facilities such as laundries, gyms, bin rooms, lounges and pool areas are used by many people, often in close contact, and the same surfaces are touched again and again. Hygiene in those spaces protects residents from contamination and protects the building from complaints, odours and pests. Before cleaning a facility, identify what it is, who uses it and what its own rules say. Some facilities have posted hours, booking systems, equipment rules or cleaning schedules. Follow those rules, and do not use a facility that is closed for maintenance.

Separate the work by area. A bin room is a high-contamination area, a laundry has wet surfaces and lint, and a gym has sweat, handles and equipment that needs its own approved product. Use dedicated tools for each area. A mop or cloth used in a bin room should never be used in a laundry or a gym, because it carries the contamination with it. Store each set of tools separately, and use a colour or label system where the building uses one. The colour system in a training example is an example only, not a standard.

A pool area is a special case. Pool and spa water quality, chemical handling and access rules are set by the owner, the manager and the regulator for the jurisdiction. This lesson does not cover pool water treatment, and it does not authorise any pool work. If your task includes the surrounds of a pool, follow the manager's instructions and the approved method, and stop at the water line unless the work has been defined and approved separately.

instruction.heading: Giving notice to tenants
instruction.body: Tenants should know in advance when a facility will be cleaned, closed or restricted. Give notice of work and closures in the way the building manager has agreed, which may be a printed notice, an email, a message through the building app or a sign at the entrance. The notice should state the facility, the date, the start and end times, and whether the facility is closed or only restricted. Where the work can change the way people reach their home or use a service, say so clearly, and offer the manager's contact details for questions. Give the notice in time for the people affected to plan. Keep a copy of the notice, the method it was sent by, and the date and time it was posted or sent. A notice that is not given in time, or cannot be shown to have been given, leaves residents surprised and gives the manager no evidence to rely on.

instruction.heading: Reporting damage, contamination and unsafe conditions
instruction.body:
Report damage, contamination, blocked drains, pest activity, leaking pipes and unsafe conditions to the building manager at once. Give the location, what you saw, when you saw it and whether anyone is at risk. Where a condition is unsafe, close the area off with signs and barriers, and keep people out until the manager confirms it is safe. Do not attempt repairs to equipment, drains, appliances or fittings in the facility, because repairs belong to the person responsible for the equipment.

Record what you found and the time, with a photograph where the building's photo rules allow it. Where the same problem appears again, record each occurrence so that the manager can see the pattern. A written record protects both the cleaner and the building, and it stops a report being lost between the cleaner and the manager.

procedure: Check the facility's rules and whether it is open or closed for maintenance before starting.
Use dedicated tools and approved products for each facility, and store them separately.
Keep bin rooms and wet areas separate from the other facilities, and clean them last where the schedule allows.
Agree the notice of work or closure with the manager, give it in the agreed way and in time, and keep a copy.
Report damage, contamination, blocked drains, pests and unsafe conditions to the manager at once.
Close off any unsafe area with signs and barriers, and record the time, the finding and the notice given.

workedExamples.situation: A bin room is overflowing, a drain in the bin room is blocked, and tenants are due to use the laundry in an hour.
workedExamples.reasoning: Keep the bin room and the blocked drain closed off with signs and barriers, and do not try to clear the drain. Report both to the manager at once, with the time and what you saw. Ask the manager to decide whether the laundry is affected, and to give tenants notice in the agreed way if it is. Keep a copy of the notice, and record the time, the finding and the closure in the visit record.

workedExamples.situation: A cleaner is asked to use the same mop that was used on the bin room floor to clean the laundry floor, because it is the only mop on the trolley.
workedExamples.reasoning: Do not use the same mop. Stop the laundry clean until a dedicated mop and bucket are available, or ask the manager to supply them. Record the request and the reason for stopping. Use the dedicated tools for each area in every visit, and do not carry the contamination from one facility to the next.

equipmentAndPpe: Dedicated mops, cloths and buckets for each shared facility, stored separately.
Approved products for each area, each with its label and SDS on hand.
Gloves and eye protection as the SDS requires.
Signs and barriers for closing off a facility.
Notice template agreed with the manager, and a copy record.
Visit record and incident note for reporting damage or unsafe conditions.

commonErrors.error: Using the same mop or cloth in the bin room and the laundry.
commonErrors.prevention: Use dedicated tools for each facility, and store them separately.

commonErrors.error: Giving no notice of a closure, or giving it too late to be useful.
commonErrors.prevention: Agree the notice with the manager, give it in the agreed way and in time, and keep a copy.

commonErrors.error: Repairing a drain, an appliance or a fitting yourself.
commonErrors.prevention: Report the fault to the manager, close off the area, and leave the repair to the person responsible.

commonErrors.error: Cleaning a pool area beyond the approved scope.
commonErrors.prevention: Stay within the agreed scope, and refer any pool water or chemical question to the manager.

commonErrors.error: Telling the manager about a problem verbally only.
commonErrors.prevention: Report in writing, with the location, time and photographs where allowed.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Chemicals used in shared facilities must be managed under the label and the SDS. A person conducting a business or undertaking must keep a hazardous chemicals register where hazardous chemicals are used, handled or stored, with the current SDS for each listed chemical, kept at the workplace where workers and others who may be affected can readily reach it. Certain exclusions apply, including some consumer products and unopened chemicals in transit (Safe Work Australia, hazardous chemicals register page; no date shown). The internal chemical reference for the business is not a substitute for this register.

Workers must be able to get the SDS for each chemical easily, and copies must be kept for chemicals used in the register. The page states exceptions for chemicals in transit, unopened retail products and household-quantity consumer products (Safe Work Australia, using safety data sheets page; no date shown).
This lesson does not authorise pool water work or chemical treatment of pool water.

qualityStandard: Dedicated tools are used for each facility in the simulation, and the tools are stored separately.
The notice of work or closure is agreed with the manager, given in the agreed way, and a copy is kept in the case study.
The blocked drain and overflow are reported at once, and the area is closed off, in the case study.
No repair is attempted on a drain, appliance or fitting by the cleaner.
documentationEvidence: Tenant notice and a copy, with the date, the method and the time given or posted.
Facility visit record with the time, the area, the tools used and the products used.
Incident or defect report for each damage, contamination, drain or unsafe condition, with the manager informed and the area closed off.
Record of each stop, such as a request to use shared tools, and the outcome.
summary: Use dedicated tools and approved products for each shared facility, and keep bin rooms and wet areas separate.
Give tenants notice of work and closures in the agreed way, in time, and keep a copy.
Report damage, contamination and unsafe conditions at once, close off the area, and do not attempt repairs.

knowledgeChecks.question: Why should a mop used in a bin room not be used in a laundry?
options: It carries contamination from one facility to another
It makes the laundry floor look dirty to users
It is too heavy to use in the laundry room with the crew
It only matters in gyms and pools and sports

knowledgeChecks.question: A blocked drain and an overflowing bin room are found before the laundry opens. What is correct?
options: Clear the drain yourself, because it is quick and easy to do on the day with the crew
Ignore it until after the laundry closes for the night and the whole long weekend ahead
Close off the areas, report both to the manager at once, and record the time and the finding
Use more product to flush the drain and the floor of the bin room and the laundry

knowledgeChecks.question: What must be kept as evidence of a closure notice?
options: Nothing, because the notice was given verbally to the staff
A copy of the notice, with the method and the date and time it was given
Only the manager's signature on the notice, the date and the room number
The cleaner's personal phone number and name on the sheet of paper and the bin
